title: One Twenty Vine: 242 Apartments Approved for Arena District Lot
author: CRE News Staff
excerpt: Nationwide Realty Investors won Columbus Downtown Commission approval for One Twenty Vine, a 242-unit apartment plan on an Arena District lot at 154 Vine Street.
answer_summary: Nationwide Realty Investors won Columbus Downtown Commission approval on September 22, 2026 for One Twenty Vine, a two-building, 242-unit apartment project on an Arena District parking lot at 154 Vine Street. The design clears review, but the project still needs building permits, and no construction date has been set.
meta_description: The Columbus Downtown Commission approved One Twenty Vine, Nationwide Realty Investors' 242-unit, two-building apartment plan for an Arena District parking lot.
body:
Nationwide Realty Investors won Columbus Downtown Commission approval on September 22, 2026 for One Twenty Vine, a two-building, 242-unit apartment project on an Arena District parking lot at 154 Vine Street. The design clears review, but the project still needs building permits, and no construction date has been set.

## How the Arena District lot would be built

The Columbus Downtown Commission, the city board that signs off on the design of downtown buildings, approved the project's design at its September 22, 2026 meeting, as reported by the [Columbus Navigator](https://www.columbusnavigator.com/one-twenty-vine-arena-district-apartments/) and [NBC4](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/arena-district-parking-lot-slated-123000614.html). Wood framing over a concrete podium is a common way to add height at lower cost than all-concrete construction, and the enclosed ground-floor parking keeps cars off the street wall.

Plans call for two seven-story buildings, each with five floors of wood framing over a two-story podium, rising to a parapet of just over 83 feet. The 242 apartments would sit above a ground floor holding a leasing office, a fitness center, a resident lounge, and 56 enclosed parking spaces, with 10 bicycle spaces and no retail. A third-floor skywalk would connect the buildings to the neighboring Kilbourne Garage, and a shared interior courtyard would add a pool deck and outdoor gathering space.

## A surface parking lot slated for housing

The buildings would replace a gravel parking lot on the block bounded by Vine, Spruce, Armstrong, and Kilbourne streets, where nine parcels and portions of the surrounding right-of-way would be combined and the site readdressed from 154 Vine Street to 120 Vine Street. The site is a paid surface lot today, one of the gravel blocks that still interrupt the Arena District's street grid near Nationwide Arena.

A CREN check of the city's public building-permit records on October 1, 2026 found no new-structure permit on file for 154 or 120 Vine Street, matching a project that has cleared design review but not yet reached the construction stage.

## Nationwide's second building on Vine Street

The same partnership built Two Twenty Vine, a 124-unit apartment building immediately west at 220 Vine Street, whose new-structure permit the city issued on December 5, 2023. The new project would roughly double that unit count on the adjacent block, extending Nationwide Realty Investors' build-out of the Vine Street corridor beside Nationwide Arena.

Nationwide Realty Investors is the development arm of Nationwide Insurance and has led the Arena District's build-out from rail yards and parking lots into offices, apartments, and entertainment.

## What the records confirm and what they leave open

CREN matched the unit count and approval date against two independent news accounts and verified the site's permit status and the neighboring building's 2023 permit directly in the City of Columbus [building-permit dataset](https://opendata.columbus.gov/datasets/columbus::building-permits), a public-domain feed released under a Creative Commons Zero waiver. The Downtown Commission's own minutes for the September 22, 2026 meeting had not been posted to the city's website as of this report, so the vote is sourced to those news accounts rather than a city document.

No construction timeline, apartment rents, or affordability set-aside has been announced, and the courtyard and amenity details come from the applicant's submitted plans as described in that coverage.

## What to watch next

The next verifiable step is a building-permit application for 120 Vine Street, which would signal a construction start and appear in the same public dataset CREN checked for this report. Until then, the plan is a design on paper, cleared for how it looks but not yet permitted to be built.

source_ledger.title: Building Permits feature service (ArcGIS REST)
source_ledger.fetch_note: Queried this CC0 ArcGIS feature service on October 1, 2026. A search for SITE_ADDRESS beginning '154 VINE' or '120 VINE' returned only a 2014 electrical permit at 154 Vine St and a 2021 commercial MEP permit at 120 Vine St, and no 'New Structure' permit for either address, consistent with a project that has cleared design review but not filed for construction. A query for new-structure permits on Vine Street in ZIP 43215 returned '220 VINE ST | Multi Family - New Structure | issued 2023-12-05 | 124 units', confirming Two Twenty Vine's unit count and permit date.

source_ledger.title: 242-Unit Apartment Building Proposed For Arena District Parking Lot
source_ledger.fetch_note: Full article fetched October 1, 2026 (byline James Arney, published September 24, 2026). Confirms 242 units; future address 120 Vine St (from 154 Vine St); block bounded by Vine, Spruce, Armstrong and Kilbourne; nine parcels plus right-of-way combined; seven stories as a two-story base with five stories above; parapet just over 83 feet; residential only, no retail; first-floor leasing office, fitness center, resident lounge and 56 enclosed parking spaces; third-floor skywalk to the Kilbourne Garage; interior courtyard with a pool; owner HP Land Development LTD (a Hamilton Parker affiliate) with Nationwide Realty Investors as development partner; architect The Columbus Architectural Studio; Downtown Commission approval Tuesday, September 22, 2026; building permits the next requirement; no construction timeline announced; Two Twenty Vine (124 apartments) built immediately west by the same partnership.

source_ledger.title: Arena District parking lot slated for 242 apartments
source_ledger.fetch_note: Full NBC4/WCMH article fetched October 1, 2026 via its Yahoo News syndication (byline Thomas Cobb, WCMH Columbus, published September 28, 2026). An independent newsroom from S3; corroborates 242 apartments across two seven-story buildings (five wood floors over a two-story podium) at 154 Vine St (to be 120 Vine St); nine parcels plus right-of-way; 56 enclosed first-floor parking spaces and 10 bicycle spaces; third-floor skywalk to the Kilbourne Garage; shared courtyard with a pool deck; Downtown Commission approval September 22, 2026; design review approved but construction permits still required; no construction timeline; Two Twenty Vine, a 124-unit building immediately west. Original publisher nbc4i.com returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch; the Yahoo syndication is the same origin, not an independent one.

image_brief.primary_request: A CREN locator map showing where the proposed One Twenty Vine apartments would rise in the Arena District, built from OpenStreetMap geometry so it needs no photograph of the gravel lot.
image_brief.editorial_idea: Place the proposed 242-unit project in its Arena District context, on a surface lot just east of the developer's existing Two Twenty Vine and a few blocks from Nationwide Arena, so readers see the block-by-block infill pattern without a copyrighted rendering or an unavailable site photo.
story_anchors: 242-unit, two-building apartment project proposed at 120 Vine Street
immediately east of Nationwide Realty Investors' existing Two Twenty Vine
an Arena District surface parking lot, blocks from Nationwide Arena
image_brief.source_asset_note: The site is a gravel surface parking lot with no rights-cleared documentary photograph available, and only the architect's copyrighted renderings exist, so CREN used a locator map built from OpenStreetMap geometry (image ladder step 2) rather than a photo or a rendering. Coordinates for the site, Two Twenty Vine, and Nationwide Arena were geocoded from OpenStreetMap on October 1, 2026, and the building-permit status was pulled from the City of Columbus open dataset.

source_review.note: OpenStreetMap geometry for the Arena District. The three map points (120/154 Vine Street, Two Twenty Vine at 220 Vine Street, and Nationwide Arena) were geocoded here on October 1, 2026 and plotted; ODbL requires the attribution printed on the image, which it carries.

The only project imagery in the news coverage is the architect's copyrighted design rendering; public display is not redistribution permission, and an official rendering may not be passed off as a site photograph, so it was not used.

image_brief.avoid: Do not present the map as a photograph or rendering of the building; do not draw a building footprint or any structure the public record does not establish; do not imply construction has started.
